pages.title: Privacy
pages.content:
Yukiki Shoes keeps the details you send us, such as your name, email address, phone number and usual size, only to answer your message or confirm a fitting. We do not pass them on.

If you ask for Letters from the shelf, we keep your email address to send one short letter a month, and we remove it when you write to ask us to stop. Write to hello@yukikishoes.example for any request about your details.

posts.title: Why we measure both feet, every time
posts.excerpt: A single size on one foot is not a record we can fit from, so every appointment at Yukiki Shoes starts by measuring both.
posts.content:
At 10:10 in every fitting we measure both feet, and we write them down as two sets of numbers. Length, width, heel, and instep. The card stays on the counter while you try a pair, and it is what we read again if you come back for a second pair or for a resole years later. Yukiki Shoes has worked this way since Mara Lindqvist opened the shop in 2011. The appointment is 45 minutes. Measuring is the second step, after you arrive at 10:00 and before you try anything at 10:20.

People often arrive with one size in mind. It is the size printed in a pair they already own, usually the shoes they wear most, which we do ask you to bring. That number is a clue. It is not a measurement of the foot that will stand on our stool today, in the socks you usually wear. Socks change the fit. So does the last. A size that felt right in a soft shoe can sit short on the Arden oxford, or long on the Wren loafer. We would rather spend the minutes at 10:10 than discover the difference at 10:35, halfway down the shop floor.

The two feet are rarely identical. Sometimes the difference is small enough that one size still works. Sometimes it is a full size, or a half size, and a single pair forces one foot to compromise. We keep sizes from 35 to 47, including half sizes, so the card can name those differences precisely. When the numbers diverge, we fit split sizes. The pair we use most often for that is the Arden oxford, the round-toe standard last, at €265. A groom came in for a wedding pair with one foot larger than the other. We did not average the two feet into a middle size. We measured both, fitted the Arden in split sizes, and he walked the floor at 10:35 before anyone called it done.

The same habit matters when the feet match and the days do not. A nurse on 12-hour shifts needed a derby that would not press a wide forefoot by the end of the day. The Hollis last is cut for that forefoot, and the Hollis derby is €245. Measuring both feet still came first. A wide forefoot on one side and a narrower one on the other would have made a single wide pair a guess. She stood for the measurement in the socks she wears on shift, because a thin sock kept for best would have given us a polite, wrong card.

We also measure again when an old pair comes back. A walker brought a nine-year-old Moor Chelsea boot to the bench. The Moor last is the high-instep shape, and the boot is €290 when new. The upper still followed the foot, and the sole was finished. Ravi Mehta does a full leather resole for €85, with the pair ready in 10 working days. Before that job was accepted, we looked at both feet again. Nine years is long enough for one foot to change, and a resole on a pair that no longer matches is a careful waste of a good upper. The first stretch on a pair bought here is free. A later stretch and adjust is €20. Neither replaces the measurement.

The six lasts only help after the card exists. Arden for a standard round toe, Hollis for a wide forefoot, Wren for a narrow heel, Moor for a high instep, Fen for a soft square toe, Teal for low volume. Trying all six on an unmeasured foot would use the whole appointment and still not tell us which foot we had fitted. The clock is fixed: arrive, measure, try, walk, decide. By 10:45 you know whether the pair on the stool is the pair that should leave the shelf.

If you book, bring those usual socks and the shoes you wear most. The fee is €20, credited to any pair. The stool is at 14 Lantern Row, Halden, and there is only one of them, so the slot is yours alone for the 45 minutes.

posts.title: Fitting the Hollis for a twelve-hour shift
posts.excerpt: A nurse on twelve-hour shifts came in for a pair she could stand in. The Hollis derby, on the wide-forefoot last, was walked on the test strip before she decided.
posts.content:
A nurse on twelve-hour shifts booked the 14:00 slot on a Thursday. Both feet were measured, and the right foot was a half size larger. The fitter, Tomas Okafor, put her in the Hollis derby, the wide-forefoot last, because the toes needed room across the front of the shoe.

At the stool the heel and instep were checked while she sat. Then she walked the shop-floor test strip in the pair, which is the part of the appointment that tells the truth: a pair that looks right in the chair can feel different on the floor.

She decided at 14:45. The Hollis derby is €245, and the €20 fitting was credited against it.

posts.title: Resoling a nine-year-old Moor
posts.excerpt: A walker brought back a nine-year-old Moor Chelsea boot. A full leather resole takes ten working days and is collected on Tuesday.
posts.content:
A walker came in with a Moor Chelsea boot bought nine years ago. The upper was still sound; the sole had worn through at the ball. Ravi Mehta, who runs the repair bench, took the boot in on a Tuesday and gave a collection date ten working days later.

What a resole involves

A full leather resole is €85. The old sole is taken off, the welt is checked, and a new leather sole is stitched and finished. A heel block is €35 if the heel has worn as well, and a stretch and adjust is €20, with the first stretch free when it comes with a pair.

Repairs are collected on Tuesday, because the shop is closed on Monday.

products.name: Arden oxford
products.short: Round toe, standard fit. The pair we split into two sizes when one foot is larger.
products.description: The Arden oxford is built on the Arden last: a round toe in a standard fit. It is fitted at the stool in a forty-five-minute appointment, and the €20 fitting is credited to the pair.

products.name: Hollis derby
products.short: Wide forefoot. The derby for long days on your feet.
products.description: The Hollis derby is cut on the Hollis last for a wide forefoot, so the toes have room across the front. Walk the shop floor in the pair before you decide.

products.name: Wren loafer
products.short: Narrow heel. The loafer that stays on without a lace.
products.description: The Wren loafer is made on the Wren last, shaped for a narrow heel, so the back of the shoe stays with the foot.

products.name: Moor Chelsea boot
products.short: High instep. The Chelsea boot for winter and long walks.
products.description: The Moor Chelsea boot is made on the Moor last, with room over a high instep. It resoles well: a nine-year-old pair is a normal job at the bench.

products.description: Arrive, measure, try, walk and decide in forty-five minutes. Slots are 10:00, 11:30, 14:00, 15:30 and 17:00, with 18:30 on Thursday. The fee is credited to any pair you take.
